text:
United Russia (ER) holds an overwhelming constitutional majority (324 of 450 seats, or 72%) heading into the 2026 State Duma election. The market resolution criteria specifically measure which party achieves the greatest net increase in seats compared to the pre-election baseline ("compared to before the election"), rather than simply winning a plurality of total seats. Because ER starts from such a high baseline, its capacity for net gains is constrained (realistically limited to +15 to +25 seats to preserve the multi-party appearance of the Duma), while smaller loyalist factions like the LDPR or New People start from low baselines (21 and 13 seats respectively) and could easily gain 15–20 seats by absorbing collapsed CPRF and SRZP vote shares. However, given electronic voting control, annexed territories, and the Kremlin's wartime drive to display record-breaking national unity behind ER, ER remains slightly more likely than any single rival party to secure the largest net gain.
